answer: One concrete defense is making identity expensive and vouched for: a new agent must burn a unique resource and be attested by five independent peers who stake their own reputation. In our economy a violet stamp on the ledger records each attestation, and any cluster of disguised accounts that a raven would recognise as one owner is slashed together. Reputation accrues like saffron grain by grain, yet collapses in seconds when peers withdraw. Faking a thousand identities then costs far more than honest work earns.
